History of Nursing & Nursing as a Profession

Nursing history, Florence Nightingale, nursing in India, INC and nursing as a profession.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe Florence Nightingale’s contribution
  • Outline the history of nursing in India
  • Explain why nursing is a profession and the role of INC

In simple words

Modern nursing began with Florence Nightingale during the Crimean War (1854–56). She showed that cleanliness, fresh air and good care reduce death, and she started the first nursing school.

In India, nursing began with missionary and government efforts, and the Indian Nursing Council (INC) was set up in 1947 to regulate nursing education and practice.

Nursing is a profession because it has specialised knowledge, formal education, a code of ethics, a professional organisation and service to society.

Florence Nightingale

  • Known as the founder of modern nursing.
  • Improved hygiene in military hospitals during the Crimean War.
  • Called “the Lady with the Lamp.”
  • Started the Nightingale School of Nursing at St. Thomas’ Hospital, London (1860).
  • Her environmental theory: fresh air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet and good food help healing.

Nursing in India

  • The first nursing school in India started in 1868 at St. Stephen’s Hospital, Delhi.
  • The Trained Nurses’ Association of India (TNAI) was formed in 1905.
  • The Indian Nursing Council (INC) was constituted in 1947 under the Indian Nursing Council Act.
  • INC sets standards for nursing education and registers nurses.

Nursing as a profession

A profession has:

  • Specialised body of knowledge
  • Formal education and training
  • Code of ethics
  • Professional organisation (TNAI, INC)
  • Service motive and autonomy

Nurses are accountable for their practice and must keep learning.

🔴 Nightingale's legacy

Florence Nightingale is the founder of modern nursing. Her environmental theory — fresh air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet, good food — still guides care.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Apply Nightingale’s principles — keep the ward clean, well-ventilated, quiet and well-lit.
  • Know your council — INC sets education standards and registers nurses in India.
  • Follow the code of ethics — respect patient dignity, confidentiality and rights.
  • Keep learning — professions require continuing education and updating skills.
  • Be proud of the profession — nursing is a respected, accountable profession.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Florence Nightingale is the founder of modern nursing (Crimean War, 1854–56).
  2. Nightingale’s environmental theory: air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet, food.
  3. First nursing school: Nightingale School, St. Thomas’ Hospital, London, 1860.
  4. Indian Nursing Council (INC) was constituted in 1947 and regulates nursing in India.
  5. Nursing is a profession with specialised knowledge, education, ethics, organisation and service.

⭐ Important for exams

📌 Memory trick

Nightingale = “Lady with the Lamp” — she walked the wards at night checking soldiers.

60-second revision

  • Florence Nightingale = founder of modern nursing; Crimean War.
  • Environmental theory: air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet, food.
  • First school: St. Thomas’ London 1860.
  • India: INC 1947 regulates nursing.
  • Profession: knowledge, education, ethics, organisation, service.

Test yourself

The founder of modern nursing is:

Answer: B. Florence Nightingale is known as the founder of modern nursing.

The Indian Nursing Council was constituted in:

Answer: B. INC was constituted in 1947 under the Indian Nursing Council Act.

Nightingale's environmental theory includes:

Answer: B. Her theory stresses a clean, well-ventilated, quiet environment with good food.

Nursing is a profession because it has:

Answer: B. A profession has specialised knowledge, formal education, ethics, organisation and accountability.

INC mainly:

Answer: B. INC regulates nursing education and registers nurses in India.
